title: 6 Things That Dropshipping Gurus Do Not Tell You As Beginner
summary: Debunker article: six things dropshipping gurus omit, from faked lifestyles and edited screenshots to affiliate-biased reviews and free alternatives to paid courses.

assertions.quote: It is possible to lease a car. You don't have to own it.

verdicts.note: Rented cars, houses and jets are documented in exposes of course sellers; the display proves nothing about income.

assertions.quote: Most companies offering to teach you how to become a successful drop shipper are making their money selling you and others their training programs.

verdicts.note: Several course sellers have disclosed that course revenue exceeded their business revenue, and regulators have made the same finding.

assertions.quote: starting a dropshipping store is like starting any other ecommerce store; it is a real business!

verdicts.note: Fulfillment is outsourced but customer acquisition, support and competition are the same as for any retailer.

Automators' coaching pitched dropshipping as risk-free because inventory is bought as needed; the FTC calls that deceptive given the routine store suspensions and terminations, supporting that it is not easy money.

assertions.quote: you can sell a product one by one without needing to go to a bulk supplier
this means that they could be biased while reviewing the course

verdicts.note: Commissioned reviewers face a clear conflict of interest, and referral programs are a standard course-marketing tactic.

assertions.quote: They might be spending $40,000 on advertisement and product costs.

verdicts.note: Sales dashboards show gross revenue; profit after ads is typically a fraction, and fabricated screenshots are documented.

assertions.quote: Purchasing a dropshipping course is like purchasing a second-hand book with a 10x markup

verdicts.note: Platform docs, free guides and videos cover the same material; the course adds structure, not secrets.

assertions.quote: you will probably make a lot of mistakes while learning more, which will probably cost you money

verdicts.note: A framing about learning, not a measurable prediction.
